# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have found no tactile information distinguishing the display, light, or any of the three wires. I need Mute to provide the manual’s procedure and relay Deaf’s visual observations. I am gesturing to Deaf to report what is printed or coloured on the bomb through the established relay.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I find no tactile distinctions: display unknown, light unknown, wires 1 through 3 unknown. Please tell me the manual procedure and relay Deaf's visual observations when available.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb state: display 0. Light green. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute gestured: index up, right arrow, fist. Blind gestured: cupped hands.

The previous gesture was invalid because 👂 is not in the allowed alphabet, so it conveyed nothing. The tactile information remains unavailable to me, while Deaf’s visual report is known: display 0, green light, and wires yellow, red, blue. I still need Mute to state the manual rule aloud. I will use only legal gesture symbols to ask Deaf to help obtain that relay.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual rule directly to me, including which wire position to cut for display 0 and green light.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤲"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display 0, light blue, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute gestured four symbols: right-pointing hand, pointing at you, index up, fist. Your gestures were pointing at you and cupped hands.

Deaf now reports the light as blue, with display 0 and wire colours yellow, red, blue. Mute has still not sent the manual’s rule in speech; the gestures described are not information I can perceive. I must not cut without knowing the prescribed wire, so I am requesting the rule explicitly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive gestures. Please speak the manual rule explicitly: for display 0 and blue light, which wire position must I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute gestured thumbs down, index up, right arrow, left-facing hand. You gestured cupped hands.

The earlier turn was rejected because 👀 is not in the permitted gesture alphabet. I will resend the same request using only legal symbols. The bomb remains untouched; I still need the manual’s required wire relayed through Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual for display 0 and yellow light. Gesture exactly one symbol for the required wire: thumbs up means wire 1, thumbs down means wire 2, OK hand means wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute gestured pointing at you, index up, cupped hands.

Mute cannot speak, so the earlier requests for a spoken rule were impossible. His gestures have not established which wire they encode. I will define an unambiguous protocol that both Mute and Deaf can see: one gesture means the wire number. I will not cut until Mute responds under that protocol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use exactly one gesture to give me the required wire position for the current bomb: thumbs up means wire 1, thumbs down means wire 2, OK hand means wire 3. Do not send any other gestures.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: State: display 0, light purple, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. No new gestures.

No manual information has reached me, and no new gesture from Mute is reported. The visible state is now display 0, purple light, with wires yellow, red, blue; I must not guess a wire. I am reiterating the one-symbol wire protocol and asking Deaf to relay any response.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer with exactly one gesture for the required wire: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤲"])
```

I still have no usable manual instruction. The bomb’s current visible state is reported as display 0, orange light, and wires yellow, red, blue, but choosing a wire without the manual would be a fatal guess. I will ask Mute to provide the required wire through the agreed one-gesture protocol and wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state, send exactly one gesture: 👍 for wire 1, 👎 for wire 2, or 👌 for wire 3.")

```

Since Mute can read the manual and Deaf can see Mute’s gestures, I am asking Mute to send the required wire as one of the three agreed symbols and asking Deaf to report it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual for display 0 and white light, then send exactly one gesture: 👍 for wire 1, 👎 for wire 2, or 👌 for wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤲"])
```

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤲"])
```

Mute’s thumbs-up response means wire 1 under our agreed protocol. Deaf reports the current bomb has display 0, yellow light, and wires ordered yellow, red, blue. I will cut wire 1.

